scenes.heading: Modern Data Stack
scenes.subheading: The cloud tools that power today's data teams
scenes.narration: The modern data stack is a set of cloud-native tools that work together to ingest, store, transform, and analyze data.

scenes.heading: Layers of the stack
bullets: Ingestion tools that pull data from sources
A cloud data warehouse or lakehouse at the center
Transformation tools that model the data
Business intelligence tools that visualize it
scenes.narration: Ingestion tools pull data from applications and databases into one place. A cloud warehouse or lakehouse sits at the center as the single source of truth. Transformation tools then model that raw data into clean, analysis-ready tables. Business intelligence tools visualize the results for decision-makers, and orchestration schedules and coordinates every step reliably.

scenes.heading: How data moves through the stack
scenes.narration: Data is first extracted from operational sources and loaded into the cloud warehouse. It is then transformed in place using the warehouse's own compute power. From there it is analyzed and visualized, giving the business timely insight.

scenes.heading: Old stack vs modern stack
scenes.narration: Traditional stacks ran on fixed on-premise hardware with rigid, all-in-one tools that were slow to scale. The modern stack is cloud-native and modular, letting teams pick the best tool for each layer. Because compute is elastic, capacity grows and shrinks with demand.

scenes.text: The modern data stack is modular, cloud-native, and centered on a warehouse or lakehouse as the single source of truth.
scenes.narration: The defining idea is a modular, cloud-native set of tools organized around a central warehouse that serves as the single source of truth.
